verdict.rationale: Glama publishes a documented OpenAPI 3.0.3 "Glama MCP API" with /v1 paths for servers and connectors. It is advertised from llms.txt and an RFC 9727 API catalog, and backed by a hosted reference (e.g. list-mcp-servers) with code samples, so an agent can search the catalog and inspect server capabilities programmatically. The 404s on generic OpenAPI paths only show the spec lives at a different path, not that the API is missing. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of a tool-level listing endpoint (tool discovery is only implied by "inspect their capabilities"), and independent hands-on corroboration of agents querying the directory API.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can query the platform's registry or catalog through a documented API to discover servers and tools programmatically

citations.quote: Glama publishes an OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for its MCP directory API (info title "Glama MCP API", /v1 paths for servers, connectors, instances, usage)
Search Glama's curated catalog of open-source servers and remote connectors, inspect their capabilities, and keep your own directory synchronized.

The RFC 9727 API catalog (application/linkset+json) links the machine spec (service-desc) and the hosted reference (service-doc), completing a fully machine-discoverable chain from the well-known path.
